_gate.sizing_note: 250, not 200. At n=200 a ZERO-error sweep gives a 95% lower bound of 0.9851 -- it clears 0.98, but a single wrong match drops it to 0.9765 and the claim fails. 250 survives one error (0.9812). The binding constraint is the error budget, not the sample size. See docs/decisions.md ADR-0015.

_needed.why: Every row is an identity established outside the resolver's own catalogs -- either elsewhere in this repository (`verified_from`) or from external research (`source: external_research`). The remainder is not invented: generating candidates from the catalogs the resolver reads would make the precision score a measurement of the catalog rather than of the resolver. Use `python -m resolve.label_cli propose` and adjudicate. CLAUDE.md: when a source cannot supply a field, delete it rather than stub it -- the same applies to a test set.

values.verified: two INDEPENDENT external sources agree on this identity. The only rows precision is scored on, and the only rows counted against the 250 gate.
values.single_source: one external source. A CANDIDATE, not ground truth. Counted and reported separately; never promoted without a second source.
values.in_repo: provenance is elsewhere in this repository (`verified_from`) rather than outside it. Not circular -- these are hand-authored fixtures, not a catalog the resolver reads -- but not independent corroboration either.
values.unstated: seeded before this field existed and the source count was never recorded. Scores nothing. Re-adjudicate or discard; back-filling a value would invent the thing the field exists to state.

_confidence.why: A single-source identity is one transcription error away from being wrong, and a precision figure computed over it measures the source rather than the resolver. Both counts are reported so the size of the candidate pool is never hidden by the size of the ground truth.
